thread:
Alex K: dropping a short follow-up proposal on 'scaling surface split' + cost accountability for Dedicated GPU pools. want quick feedback before i turn into an RFC.
Irene (runtime): nice. quick q — are we still assuming operator is purely node-lifecycle and control plane keeps intent?
Alex K: yes — operator: scale up/down nodes, manage leases, drain. control plane: admission, intent, per-tenant budgets, and fallback routing.
Maria G: what's the main pain we're trying to solve that we don't already have with existing autoscaler?
Alex K: two things: 1) unclear boundary causes racey double-scaling and cost surprises, 2) tenants have no real-time cost accounting so bursts blow committed budgets.
Samir: I like separate concerns. but we need a clear sync contract. propose an "intent ledger" + bounded admission window.
Lee (infra): concretely what does the ledger hold? tokens, cost attribution, timestamped intents?
Alex K: prototype ledger fields: tenant_id, intent_id, requested_slices, cost_tokens_reserved, created_at, expires_at, source (api/scheduler).
Irene (runtime): example intent CRD would help.
Alex K: posting snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: PoolScaleIntent
metadata:
  name: tenant-42-intent-202403
spec:
  tenantId: tenant-42
  requestedSlices: 20
  costBudgetTokens: 500
  admissionWindowSeconds: 30
  preferSpot: true
```
Samir: admissionWindowSeconds is key. operator should only act on intents with created_at older than window_start to avoid flipflop on short bursts.
Maria G: how do we handle cancellations / graceful drain if operator has already provisioned a node?
Lee (infra): operator keeps a lease reference to the intent_id. if intent expires early, operator marks node as "ephemeral-drain" and starts TTL drain (configurable).
Irene (runtime): what about cost accounting accuracy? we should charge tokens only for provisioned slice-minutes, not requested slices. need reconciliation job.
Alex K: agreed. ledger lifecycle: reserve tokens at admission, operator emits provisioned event (provisioned_slices) which deducts tokens real-time. reconcile job runs hourly to settle drift.
Samir: fallback routing: when tenant budget exhausted, control plane should route to cheaper model variant or enqueue. this must be declarative in intent response.
Maria G: can we add an intent response shape? e.g., status.blocked|admitted|fallback with reason and fallback_policy
Alex K: exactly. sample status:
```yaml
status:
  state: admitted
  provisionedSlices: 18
  fallbackPolicy: null
  costTokensCharged: 123
```
Lee (infra): operator API: watch intents CRD, act on admitted intents. expose metrics: per-tenant provisioned_slices, pending_intents, token_balance.
Irene (runtime): ops question: who owns retries when operator fails to provision? control plane should automatically retry with backoff and emit incident if > threshold.
Alex K: ops-bot should alert after 5 failed attempts per intent. also circuit-breaker: if operator reports > X failures cluster-wide, control plane throttles new admissions.
ops-bot: noted. will wire alerts for intent failures and cluster-provision-fail-rate.
deploy-bot: deploying intent CRD schema to staging in 30m :rocket:
Samir: small nit — make admissionWindowSeconds tenant-configurable to support high-frequency tenants (low-latency) vs cost-sensitive ones.
Maria G: plus add soft vs hard reservation. soft = tokens reserved but auto-fallback; hard = block if insufficient tokens.
Irene (runtime): we should also document latency SLOs implied by this split. operator actions must complete within N seconds for cold-start-sensitive tenants.
Alex K: next steps: I'll draft RFC with CRD schema, operator contract, ledger reconciliation plan, and proposed metrics/alerts. want volunteers for review: @Irene, @Lee, @Samir?
Irene (runtime): happy to review.
Lee (infra): I can take infra ops section.
Samir: i'll sanity-check admission/backoff semantics.
Alex K: thanks all. leaving the thread open for comments. :+1:
